variant_decisions.evidence: ASV's text reads 'on some have mercy', and the mapped note relegates the refuting reading to the margin ('Some ancient authorities read And some refute'), so Treg's elenchete is excluded. eleate and eleeite are orthographic forms of the same verb and both give 'have mercy'.

ASV renders three distinct groups across 1:22-23 -- 'on some have mercy, who are in doubt' (accusative diakrinomenous as the object of eleate), 'and some save, snatching them out of the fire', 'and on some have mercy with fear'. That three-clause shape excludes r02 (WH), which lacks the second 'ous de' and so folds the rescued into the doubters, and excludes r03 (RP), which has nominative diakrinomenoi and only two groups with no closing 'have mercy with fear' clause; the ASV note reports the r03 sense ('some refute while they dispute with you', cf. the alternative rendering 'while they dispute with you') as what other authorities read, i.e. not the text translated. r00-base and r01 are the same words and differ only in comma placement, which the English cannot distinguish, so the unit stays underdetermined between them and the base fallback carries the projection.
